content.text:
`out/transform.ts` is finished. It type-checks and runs cleanly on the sample patients. I also tested it with a scratch script (`out/scratch.ts`) on cases the samples don't have: hold and stop replay, a wrong-patient void, the `asOf` cutoff, restricted behavioral-health entries, unit conversion, eGFR variants and drug-caused diagnoses. Those came out as intended, but they are my own made-up cases, so they only check the logic against my reading of the docs.

Judgment calls:

- **Which items count:** an item is in scope if its `recorded` time falls on or before `asOf` in Chicago time. An item is dropped if any in-scope item lists it in `supersedes`, `retracts` or a void's `voided_items`. Dropped events are taken out before the lists are replayed, so a voided stop can't change a line.
- **Medications:**
  - Status comes from the latest event per `med_id`: start, change or resume means active, hold means held, stop means stopped.
  - A hold stays held regardless of `review_on`.
  - `status_since` is the most recent start or resume for active lines, and the start of the current hold, or the stop, otherwise.
  - Where several lines share an ingredient, I keep the one whose latest event is latest.
  - I get the ingredient by parsing the drug name: stripping salts and forms, plus a brand-to-generic table.
  - I never fill `rxnorm_ingredient`, because Northgate only stores product-level RxNorm codes.
  - A dose in tablets becomes a mass when the name gives exactly one per-tablet strength (2 × 50 mg = 100 mg).
  - Names that look like IV or infusion orders are left out as hospital-only.
- **Problems:** a removed line is dropped and a resolved line stays as resolved. All kidney-disease lines (N18.*) merge into one row; other lines merge by ICD-10 code. The CKD stage comes from the description first, then the code. A plain N18.3 gives no stage, because it doesn't say 3a or 3b. Billing and referral diagnoses are ignored, and so are list reviews.
- **Drug-caused diagnoses:** a description like "X-associated…" or an adverse-effect T-code also produces an allergy row.
  - If the description names only a drug class, I use the one matching drug in the same item if there is exactly one, otherwise the class name.
  - A T-code that names no condition gives an allergy row only, with mechanism "unknown".
  - Criticality is always "unknown" because the source doesn't assess it. You could argue ketoacidosis should be "high".
- **Allergies:**
  - The reaction type is decided from the recorded reactions first, then from Northgate's own type.
  - Mechanism follows Northgate's definitions: "allergy" means immune and "intolerance" means non-immune. ACE-inhibitor cough or angioedema is always non-immune.
  - Inactivated lines are dropped.
- **Labs:**
  - Non-numeric values such as "Result invalidated" are left out.
  - The race-coefficient eGFR variant is always dropped. The equation is read from the lab's method note first, then from Lakeview's result code.
  - Platelet and white-cell counts filed in cells/uL are divided by 1000.
  - A result whose unit I can't convert is skipped rather than guessed.
  - Results are de-duplicated by accession and component, preferring final over preliminary.
- **Vitals:** every vital set is a "clinic" row, timed at the item's `effective` in Chicago time, with the repeat BP on the same row. Height, temperature and SpO2 aren't in the view, so they're dropped.
- **Sensitivity:** a behavioral-health restriction is mapped to "mental-health". I also flag F, HIV/STI and pregnancy ICD codes even when the source doesn't mark them restricted.

- **Vitals:** every vital set is a "clinic" row, timed at the item's `effective` in Chicago time, with the repeat BP on the same row. Height, temperature and SpO2 aren't in the view, so they're dropped.
- **Sensitivity:** a behavioral-health restriction is mapped to "mental-health". I also flag F, HIV/STI and pregnancy ICD codes even when the source doesn't mark them restricted.
